Hi Michael — Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, then a bit more detail and options.

Short answers:
- Do we store prompts/outputs by default? Yes for Redwood Hosted: request payloads (prompt inputs) and model outputs are stored by default for troubleshooting, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. Default retention is 30 days.
- Storage location: Hosted data is stored in our regional cloud tenancy (primary: us-west-2 for Acme Health) with encryption at rest and in transit.
- Logs/audit trails: Request metadata, routing decisions, and platform audit logs are retained by default for 90 days.
- Opt-out / zero-retention: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support a "no-persist" or configurable retention policy (including retention=0) as part of the deployment configuration or contractual addendum. For Hosted customers we can offer shorter retention windows or a commercial agreement to reduce retention, depending on plan and compliance requirements.
- KMS/HSM: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers may use Redwoods-managed encryption keys by default; customer-managed keys are available on enterprise agreements.

More detail / clarifications:
- What is stored: For Hosted by default we store the full request payload (prompt/text input, request metadata such as model, temperature, request-id) and the model-generated output. We also persist derived telemetry (token counts, latencies) used for billing and optimization.
- Purpose of retention: storage is used for debugging, abuse detection (safety), quality monitoring, and billing reconciliation.
- Redaction/masking: We offer an optional redaction pipeline that can remove or mask PII from stored artifacts before persisting. This is configurable and we can run an initial set of redaction rules for common PHI patterns.
- Residency: We can pin data to a specific cloud region for Hosted customers and we offer Dedicated/Private deployments for full control over physical residency.
- Audit evidence & SOC2: I will share the SOC 2 summary link and our DPA (attached) in the next message.

Next steps we propose for Acme Health:
1) We can provision a short-term test environment with retention=0 for production-like traffic (Dedicated or Private) so you can validate that prompts/outputs are not persisted.
2) If you prefer Hosted, we can apply a 7-day retention window and enable our redaction pipeline for the pilot.
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical review with your security team next week to confirm DPA/BAA terms and KMS set up.

Let me know which option you prefer and available times for a security call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
